note: Official lists are written in plain words here. The meaning follows the source, and the link goes to the original wording.

eac.title: East African Community customs law (EAC Customs Management Act 2004, Second Schedule)
eac.summary: Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi share one customs law, so this list applies in all five. Each country can add its own bans on top.

source.text: Kenya Revenue Authority copy of the Second Schedule

sections.heading: Banned imports (Part A)
items: Anything banned by any other law of the country
Fake money, and fake or non-standard coins and notes
Pornography in any form, and any indecent or obscene prints, paintings, books, cards or other items
Matches made with white phosphorus
Anything using a member country's coat of arms without permission, or a copy close enough to fool people

Spirits containing harmful oils or chemicals, including thujone, star anise, benzoic aldehyde, salicylic esters, hyssop and absinthe (anise liqueurs with no more than 0.1 percent anise oil are allowed)
Narcotic drugs under international control
Hazardous waste
All soaps and cosmetics containing mercury
Used tyres for cars and light commercial vehicles

Farm chemicals: 2,4,5-T, aldrin, captafol, chlordimeform, chlorobenzilate, DDT, dieldrin, EDB, fluoroacetamide, HCH, heptachlor, hexachlorobenzene, lindane, mercury compounds, some monocrotophos products, methamidophos, phosphamidon, methyl parathion and parathion
Industrial chemicals: crocidolite (blue asbestos), PBBs, PCBs, PCTs, tris (2,3-dibromopropyl) phosphate and methyl bromide
Counterfeit goods of all kinds

sections.heading: Restricted imports, need a permit (Part B)
items: Anything controlled by any other law of the country
Postal franking machines
Traps that can kill or catch wild animals
Raw (unworked) precious metals and precious stones
Guns and ammunition
Bones, horn and horn cores, raw or simply prepared, and their powder and waste
Elephant ivory, hippo teeth and rhino horn, raw or simply prepared
Worked ivory and anything made of ivory
Tortoiseshell, whalebone, horns, antlers, hooves, claws and beaks
Coral, shells and similar materials, raw or simply prepared
Carvings and items made from bone, tortoiseshell, horn, antler, coral or mother-of-pearl
Natural sponges of animal origin
Used nuclear reactor fuel
Ozone-depleting substances (Montreal Protocol)
Genetically modified products
Fish species, or their eggs, that are not native to the region
Endangered plants and animals and their products (CITES)
Second-hand tyres (commercial casings)
Psychotropic drugs under international control
Historical artefacts
Explosives items such as percussion caps, detonators and signal flares
Parts of guns and ammunition, in metal or plastic
Armoured fighting vehicles
Telescopic sights and other gun sights, unless on or with the gun they belong to
Bows, arrows and fencing foils
Antique and collectors' guns and ammunition

nigeria.title: Nigeria Customs Service: goods whose import is absolutely banned
nigeria.summary: This is the older, permanent list in the customs law. It sits alongside the Finance Ministry list from April 2026 shown above.

source.text: US trade.gov copy of the Nigeria Customs list

sections.heading: Absolutely banned imports
items: Air pistols
Airmail photographic printing paper
All counterfeit or pirated materials and articles, including fake coins of any country
Beads made of flammable celluloid or similar material
Blank invoices
Coupons for foreign football pools or other betting
Cowries
Exhausted tea, or tea mixed with other substances
Tools for reloading gun cartridges
Indecent or obscene prints, paintings, books, cards, engravings or other items
Manilas (old brass or copper ring money)
Matches made with white phosphorus
Any material with a design likely to cause a breach of the peace or offend religious views
Meat, vegetables or other food declared unfit to eat by a health officer
Cloth, textiles and clothing bearing Koranic writing
Pistols disguised as another object
Second-hand clothing
Silver or metal coins that are not legal money in Nigeria
Nuclear, industrial and other toxic waste
Any spirit above 48.5 percent alcohol, and some spirits apart from common types such as brandy, gin, rum and whisky
Weapons made to spray a harmful liquid or gas, such as tear gas, and ammunition for them

sections.heading: Banned exports
items: Maize
Rough or sawn timber
Raw hides and skins, including wet blue and unfinished leather
Scrap metal
Unprocessed rubber latex and rubber lumps
Artefacts and antiquities
Endangered wildlife and their products, such as crocodiles, elephants and eagles
All imported goods (you cannot re-export goods that were imported)

ghana.title: Ghana Revenue Authority: import and export bans
ghana.summary: Ghana's Customs Act 2015 also bans importing right-hand drive vehicles unless the minister approves.

sections.heading: Banned imports
items: Animals or carcasses with a disease under the Diseases of Animals Act
Beads made of flammable celluloid or similar material
Raw coffee brought in by road or inland waterway
Foreign coins that are not of the proper standard
Food declared unfit to eat by a health officer
Knuckle dusters and life preservers (small clubs)
Books, newspapers and printed matter that are defamatory, scandalous or demoralising
Fake coins and fake banknotes
Indecent or obscene prints, paintings, photos, books, cards and other items
Flick knives and other knives treated as dangerous weapons
Anything banned by any other law of Ghana

sections.heading: Restricted imports, with who gives the permit
items: Currency, travellers' cheques and securities: Bank of Ghana
Rough or uncut diamonds: Ministry of Mines
Mercury: Ministry of Mines
Items printed to look like money: Ministry of Finance
Gambling machines: Gaming Commission
Plants, seeds, soil and anything that can carry plant disease: Ministry of Food and Agriculture
Guns, ammunition and explosives: Ministry of the Interior
Handcuffs and key-cutting machines: Ministry of the Interior
Weapons that spray a harmful liquid or gas: Ministry of the Interior
Some spirits and alcoholic drinks: Commissioner-General of the GRA
Cinema films: Commissioner-General, and only at some ports

sections.heading: Banned exports
items: Round logs of 12 timber species, including rosewood
Narcotics and psychotropic drugs
African grey parrots
Endangered animal species
Currency above USD 10,000
Rattan canes and bamboo
Obscene and pornographic material
Anything banned by international law

gambia.title: Gambia Revenue Authority: Customs and Excise Act 2010

sections.heading: Banned imports (section 38)
items: Fake or non-standard coins and banknotes
Indecent items, including pornography
Guns and ammunition without a licence
Illegal drugs
Expired food, drinks and medicines
Waste and sludge
Any organic phosphorus compound
Goods meant to break someone's intellectual property rights, such as fakes
Asbestos in any form
Ivory and ivory items, wild animal skins, snake skins, turtle shell items and wild plants
Plastic bags
Anything banned by an international treaty the Gambia has signed
Live fish, except native species with a licence
Goods that fail Gambia Standards Bureau checks

sections.heading: Restricted imports, need a permit
items: Guns: licence from the Ministry of the Interior
Key-cutting machines
Handcuffs: licence from the Ministry of the Interior
Tear gas
Live birds and animals from other African countries
Camera drones: clearance from the Ministry of Information and Communication
Military gear
Non-native live fish: licence from the Fisheries Ministry

sections.heading: Banned exports (section 99)
items: Guns and ammunition sent by post
Illegal drugs
Asbestos
Anything else banned by Gambian law

south-africa.title: South African Revenue Service: what travellers cannot bring in
south-africa.summary: This is the traveller version. The full list for traders is a spreadsheet of tariff codes on the SARS website.

sections.heading: Banned
items: All narcotic and psychotropic drugs, and habit-forming drugs such as cannabis, heroin, cocaine, Mandrax and ecstasy, plus anything used to take them
Fully automatic, military and unnumbered guns
Explosives and fireworks
Weapons of mass destruction
Poisons and other toxic substances
Cigarettes weighing more than 2 kg per 1,000
Goods with a trade mark or trade description used against the law, such as counterfeit goods
Illegal copies of anything protected by copyright
Goods made in prisons

sections.heading: Restricted, need a permit or must be declared
items: South African banknotes above R25,000, gold coins, coin and stamp collections, and raw gold
Endangered plants and animals, alive or dead, and anything made from them
All plants and plant products, such as seeds, flowers, fruit, honey, margarine and vegetable oils
All animals, birds and poultry and their products, such as dairy, butter and eggs
Medicines beyond three months' supply for personal use, which need a doctor's letter or prescription

zambia.title: Zambia Revenue Authority: passenger clearance leaflet

sections.heading: Banned imports
items: Fake coins or banknotes
Anything indecent, obscene or objectionable
Pirated or counterfeit goods
Goods made in prisons
Spirits containing harmful extracts, essences or chemicals
Anything banned under any other law
Narcotic drugs, which will lead to prison
Methadone, unless you have a licence or permit

sections.heading: Restricted, need a licence or permit
items: Farm produce such as fresh fruit, vegetables, meat and livestock, and plants
Wheat grain and seed
Medicines and drugs
Mineral ores and precious stones
Guns and ammunition
Pets

mauritius.title: Mauritius Revenue Authority: banned and restricted goods
mauritius.summary: The MRA says this list is not complete. Items most likely to affect travellers are listed first.

source.text: MRA prohibited and restricted goods list

sections.heading: Banned tobacco and nicotine products (2022 rules)
items: E-cigarettes and vapes, their e-liquids, devices and accessories
Any other nicotine product made to replace tobacco, except nicotine replacement therapy prescribed by a doctor
Heated tobacco products and their devices
Hookah (waterpipes) and waterpipe tobacco
Flavoured tobacco
Smokeless tobacco
Roll-your-own tobacco, papers and filters
Covers or cases made to hide the health warnings on cigarette packs

sections.heading: Other banned imports
items: Fake coins
Goods with a false maker's name, trade mark or place of origin
Ivory and tortoiseshell
Toy pistols and guns that fire projectiles, and caps for toy guns
Underwater fishing guns (spearguns)
Laser pointers and pens of 1 milliwatt or more
Firecrackers known as pétards rapés
Any goods, paintings or designs likely to outrage a religion or good morals
Cosmetics containing vitamin K1
White phosphorus matches
Batteries containing mercury
Sweets and gum shaped like cigarettes
Jelly sweets in mini cups or capsules containing konjac or certain thickeners
Toy motorcycle helmets, and full-face motorcycle helmets with a tinted visor
PVC teethers and teething rings
Yoyo water ball toys
Remoulded, recapped or regrooved car tyres
Fridges, freezers, air conditioners and aerosols using CFC or HCFC gases
Blue asbestos, PBBs, PCBs and PCTs
Aerosol sprays containing benzene
Kerosene stoves known as lampes vertes
Most ordinary incandescent light bulbs
Electric water heaters with a bare element
Bull bars for cars
Small fishing hooks
Hand-rolling machines for cigarettes
Many used car parts, such as brake linings, shock absorbers, filters and tyres
Second-hand cars outside the allowed age range (except an individual's first car)
Round logs and timber from Liberia
COVID-19 rapid antibody tests

sections.heading: Restricted, need a permit
items: Fireworks and firecrackers
Rough diamonds and raw gold
Guns, ammunition, explosives and stun torches: Police
Medicines and e-cigarette products: Pharmacy Board
Plants, plant products and sugar cane cuttings: National Plant Protection Office
Animals, including cats and dogs: Veterinary Services
Endangered plants and animals: National Parks and Conservation Service
Telecom equipment and anything that can intercept messages: ICT Authority
Hemp products such as hemp oil and hemp soap: Mauritius Standards Bureau
Plastic bags and hazardous waste: Ministry of Environment
Coin-operated gaming machines
Second-hand vehicles
